themes.name: AI-Facilitated Critical Thinking Development
themes.definition: The integration of artificial intelligence tools to actively promote, enhance, or develop critical thinking skills among students across various educational disciplines and levels, as observed through explicit mentions in the abstracts.
evidence: [Liu2024c] improve critical thinking skills among college students
[Calderón-Oliver2025] facilitating the development of critical thinking

themes.name: Challenges and Limitations in AI-Assisted Education
themes.definition: Difficulties, negative outcomes, or concerns arising from the use of AI tools in educational settings, including technical issues, over-reliance, ethical dilemmas, privacy concerns, and reduced human interaction, as explicitly stated in the abstracts.
evidence: [Klçkaya2025] challenges such as limited understanding, technical issues, and privacy concerns
[Habib2025] frequently compromising accuracy by being prone to errors and misinformation
[ElIdrissi2025] reduced peer discussion and lower average performance

themes.name: Personalized and Adaptive AI Learning Supports
themes.definition: The application of AI to provide customized feedback, adaptive learning environments, or personalized resources tailored to individual student needs, enhancing learning outcomes and engagement, as indicated in the abstracts.
evidence: [Becerra2025] provides personalized, actionable feedback tailored to individual student performance
[Liu2024c] personalized socio-scientific issues (SSIs) education model based on AI adaptive learning environments

themes.name: AI Impact on Collaboration and Peer Interaction
themes.definition: The effects of AI tools on student collaboration, peer discussions, and group dynamics, with observed impacts ranging from enhanced teamwork to reduced interaction, as described in the abstracts.
evidence: [ElIdrissi2025] reduced peer discussion and lower average performance
[Agnaou2025] explores how LLMs influence collaborative learning

themes.name: Development of Creativity and Problem-Solving Skills with AI
themes.definition: The use of AI tools to foster and enhance students' creativity and problem-solving abilities in various educational contexts, as explicitly mentioned in the abstracts.
evidence: [Lee2025c] enhance students’ creativity, critical thinking and innovation
[Xiao2025] enhances students’ coding proficiency, creativity, and critical thinking
[Agnaou2025] focusing on student creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving

themes.name: Ethical and Literacy Considerations in AI Use
themes.definition: The emphasis on developing ethical awareness, AI literacy, and responsible use of AI technologies among students and educators, as highlighted in the abstracts.
evidence: [Delanoy2025] enhance their learning, critical thinking, and ethical awareness
[Chew2025] promote accessibility without compromising rigor. Through hands-on, visual-first learning tools, students explore AI ethics

data.meta_observations: Critical thinking is a dominant theme across most abstracts, often linked directly to AI integration. Challenges are frequently noted alongside benefits, indicating a balanced perspective. Mixed-methods approaches are common, but many abstracts have missing elements like quantitative data or specific methods. AI tools like ChatGPT and GenAI are prominently featured across diverse educational contexts.
data.grounding_notes: Some abstracts have quality notes indicating missing information, so evidence is limited to explicitly stated text. Quotes are verbatim from the provided abstracts. Articles list includes only keys from the closed set. For themes like critical thinking, not all articles use the exact term 'critical thinking' (e.g., Espínola2025 uses 'critical reflection', Rattanakha2025b uses 'analytical thinking'), so they are included only where terminology matches. Confidence is high for all themes due to clear evidence in multiple abstracts.
